paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: Jesus is Lord of the Sabbath, and the Sabbath was never meant to be used as a club. The Pharisees came with a rulebook. Jesus came with mercy, and He reminded them of the line "I desire mercy, not sacrifice." (Matthew 12:7) Then He says it plain: "the Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath." (Matthew 12:8)

Now look at that man with the withered hand. They used him to set a trap, and Jesus saw a man who needed help. "How much more valuable is a man than a sheep!" (Matthew 12:12) That's you, baker. Not a project, not a problem, not a bargaining chip. Jesus says it is lawful "to do good on the Sabbath," and it's lawful to do good for YOU. (Matthew 12:12)

And listen to what Matthew says about the Servant. "A bruised reed He will not break, and a smoldering wick He will not extinguish." (Matthew 12:20) So when you feel bent, or just barely glowing, you can come to Him anyway. He doesn't snap you or snuff you out. He does it quietly, until He "leads justice to victory," and "In His name the nations will put their hope." (Matthew 12:20-21)
